beats: Hook: a code suggestion that arrives after you have typed the line is useless; when does guessing ahead pay? (line_guess_snail_suggestion, the cover).

Drafts without a draft model (slides 26-27): REST looks continuations up in a datastore of past text (line_guess_phrasebook; reuse line_card_catalog); lookahead decoding keeps a pool of n-grams it collects as it goes (line_guess_snippet_jar).
Built in from the start (slide 28): multi-token prediction trains extra heads with the backbone from scratch, and the model itself gets better (Meta, ICML 2024) (line_guess_sight_reading).
DeepSeek-V3 (slide 29): chained MTP modules, each building on the one before; the second token is accepted 85-90% of the time (line_guess_relay_runners).
When it pays (slide 30): small batches (under 4-32), where the GPU is idle anyway (line_guess_taxi_vs_bus; line_spec_oven_one_cookie from L08-01 if it is in the library).
Latency-critical uses (slides 31-35, no screenshots): a chat app's first token in 200-500 ms, search answers, code completion (line_guess_chat_wait; reuse line_chat_first).
Reasoning models (slide 36): very long outputs and long contexts force small batches, and their patterns are strong: a good fit (line_guess_long_thinking).
When it does not pay (slide 37): big-batch serving for cheap tokens; the compute is already busy (line_guess_busy_kitchen).
Takeaway: guessing spends spare compute to buy speed, so first check that there is spare compute (reuse line_balance); closes the speculative-decoding lecture.
Cover (line_cover_l08_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the programmer has finished and folded their arms; the snail with the suggestion is only now crossing the desk.
